observation.visible_scene: A still alpine landscape: a broad brown, grassy mountain slope topped by a jagged ridgeline with small patches of snow sits under a pale overcast sky, and its image is mirrored almost perfectly in a glassy, dark lake that fills the lower half of the frame. A strip of dry golden grass and a cluster of dark evergreen trees occupy the lower-left foreground.
visible_changes: Across all sampled frames the mountains, ridgeline, snow patches, foreground trees and grass keep the same position relative to the frame edges, so no object translation, deformation or camera pan/zoom is detectable.
The lake surface stays a near-perfect mirror reflection throughout; no ripple propagation or change in the reflected shape is visible between the first and last frame.

A faint watermark text overlay near the centre shoreline, readable in the early frames, is no longer visible in the later frames; this is an overlay/editing change of the image, not motion within the scene.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the disappearance of the watermark marks an editing boundary or merely a fading overlay is not determinable from the excerpt.
Any wind, water movement or lighting change outside the sampled interval is unknown.
uncertain_details: Extremely subtle shifts in reflection contrast or tiny surface ripples cannot be confirmed from the discrete samples.
Static framing is inferred from background alignment; minute camera motion cannot be entirely excluded but is not evidenced.

NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
